subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What should OpenClaw's v1 durable memory lifecycle contract be for review, edit, forget, supersede, tombstone, and conflict states?
rationale: The requested behavior defines storage semantics, plugin/API behavior, operator UX, privacy expectations, and compatibility for persisted memory, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/API anchor and require an explicit v1 state model before implementation starts.

options.title: Narrow to CLI-only MVP
options.body: Limit v1 to `openclaw memory` review/edit/forget commands and defer richer plugin/API and UI flows.

options.title: Defer to Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat lifecycle curation as a wiki-layer concern for now, accepting that active memory recall and promotion remain without first-class forget/conflict semantics.

recommendation.title: Design lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/API anchor and require an explicit v1 state model before implementation starts.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core, memory-wiki, and memory-doc history makes this the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
